takeaways.headline: Singapore is the region's only front-end chipmaking hub
takeaways.body: None of the other five countries has a confirmed commercial 300mm wafer fab. For a chipmaker already in Singapore, they are not places to build a front-end fab; they matter for packaging, testing, customer support and spreading supply-chain risk.

takeaways.headline: Singapore itself is getting more crowded
takeaways.body: GlobalFoundries opened a US$4B expansion in 2023, and the US$7.8B VIS–NXP joint venture (VSMC) is due to start customer output in 2027 in the same mature-node space. More capacity next door means more competition for the same customers.

takeaways.headline: The other five attract packaging, testing and power-chip plants
takeaways.body: Recent examples: Infineon's silicon-carbide power fab in Kulim, Amkor's advanced-packaging campus in Bac Ninh, and Intel's assembly and test sites in Malaysia and Vietnam. Malaysia's cluster is the most established; Indonesia is still early.

takeaways.headline: The biggest questions can't be answered from public data
takeaways.body: Whether customers actually want capacity or support in the region, whether China+1 diversification lasts, and whether a site can get enough reliable power would change the picture most.

not_a_ranking: This is not a ranking, a score or an investment recommendation. It organizes public evidence so readers can form their own judgment.

status_definitions.credible: Activity by multiple companies that a customer could rely on today.
status_definitions.emerging: Real but early, anchored by one company, or driven by policy.
